items.name: changelog-page
items.title: Changelog page
items.description: The changelog template, built only from library items: every release newest first under a hairline, its date in capitals on the left, the change as a Funnel Display sentence, its details and a picture when there is one.
items.use_for: A website's changelog. The entries are examples drawn from what the assets say the product does, and their dates are placeholders: replace them in lib/pages/changelog.ts.
never: New colors, shadows or type sizes added to a section: use the items' props
More than one White button in a section
A release date that is not real
items.source: Built from the library (site header, creative card, footer row); the entries' sentences are the posts' own lines
items.body:
`sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`head`, `entries`); a key left out is not shown. Each entry's `image`
is a creative (an image slot, or the placeholder's `brand` and `tone`). `menus` passes the header menus (the live
card's `picture`, the use cases' `shots`).

items.name: chart
items.title: Chart
items.description: How a number is drawn: White bars per day under a total, and lines over time in the brand's series order (White, #A3A3A3, #4D4D4D, then the spectrum from Magenta to Blue). Axes from 0 on #363636 hairlines; pointing reads a value.
items.use_for: Searches per day, creatives found per category, spend over a flight. Every chart has a caption; every series is named in the legend.
never: Series colors out of order, or spectrum colors before the neutrals
Color alone to tell series apart: the third series is dashed and every series is in the legend
An axis that starts above 0
Bars that regrow on every hover: they rise once
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: Black ground, White primary, the neutral spectrum for the first series and the seven spectrum colors in their fixed order after them, DM Sans figures and capital labels at 6%, the #262626 card fill. shadcn's chart for the parts (caption, legend, tooltip).
items.body:
`lib/chart.ts` holds the series colors (`CHART_COLORS`, ten in order) and the axis helpers both flavors use; draw your
own charts with them so the order stays the brand's.

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: A yes or no that is part of a form: a 16px box in a #666666 hairline on Black that fills White with a Black check, a bar for a group partly on, and a DM Sans label beside it. Form-associated.
items.use_for: Filters a person combines, consent in a form, picking rows. A setting that takes effect at once is a switch.
never: A spectrum color for the checked box
A checkbox that acts at once without a form or an apply step
Faded labels for disabled: they go to the faint neutral
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: White on Black for what is on, neutral hairlines, the 4px small corner, DM Sans labels. shadcn's checkbox for anatomy and the indeterminate state.

items.name: close-block
items.title: Close block
items.description: The home's close: a screen-tall section with the headline, the connect menu and the quiet button in its middle, square creatives scattered around them that the light wakes from grey once, lit and leaning toward the pointer under a mouse, with a tag naming the one under it.
items.use_for: The last section of a home page: one line and the two ways to start, among the material the product indexes.
never: Third-party creatives you may not show: the defaults are Acme placeholders
Creatives over the words: the scatter keeps them clear
The sweep or the lean with reduced motion: the creatives stay in color and still
items.source: Site v3/V3Close (V3Close.tsx and .module.css, scatter.ts, CloseLight.tsx, CloseTags.tsx; content/v3/close): the seeded scatter (seed 6 wide on an 880 field, 8 on phones on 720), the field's unit the section's height (at least 640px, one screen), the words lifted by width, creatives at rest grayscale 1 and brightness 0.32, the sweep 640px wide at 16deg crossing once over 1400ms on the loop ease, the pointer's 400px reach and 4px lean, the tag 8px off the creative and 16px clear of the words; the menu opening downward; the tag leaving over 120ms; on phones the connect menu hidden and the quiet button White (globals.css [data-mcp-pair])
items.body:
Each picture is an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`); without `src` it keeps its placeholder, which carries
`data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code block
items.description: The site's tabs of code: a #262626 panel with a 56px head of tabs (a White line sliding under the chosen one) and a copy button whose label turns to Copied, over code in White with its punctuation and comments muted, scrolling across. Code and the copy button also stand alone.
items.use_for: Requests and setup steps on product, docs and resource pages (`tabs` of { id, label, code, language }); `Code` alone inside a response panel or a card; `CopyButton` beside a URL or a key.
never: Colored syntax highlighting: only the muted gray and White
Code that wraps: it scrolls across and fades at its edges
A White copy button: it is quiet
items.source: Site sections/Connect (Code.tsx, CodeTabs.tsx, CopyButton.tsx, Connect.module.css .panel, .tab, .tabLine, .codePanel, .pre, .copy): --surface panel, --radius-m; head --control-l, 4px in (8 from 768), --line-surface hairline; tabs 14/20 Medium --text-3, 12px in (16 from 768), a --stroke White line on the sliding pill; .btn--quiet .btn--s copy at 80px or wider, --radius-s, labels crossing 4px over --dur-fast; panels 16px in (24 from 768), mono --small-size

items.name: collapsible
items.title: Collapsible
items.description: A part that opens in place and pushes what follows: a quiet DM Sans Medium trigger with a muted chevron that turns, and content that grows to its height and settles in.
items.use_for: More filters under a search, the rest of a list, details a person asks for. Several questions in a stack are an accordion.
never: Hiding what most people need
A chevron that moves on hover
Animating it when it is toggled from the keyboard
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: DM Sans Medium labels, muted neutrals for secondary text, the #262626 card fill. shadcn's collapsible for anatomy and ARIA.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: A field-like trigger that opens a list to pick one option from, with a filter over it, on the #262626 overlay panel: the menus' rows, a #262626 fill on the row the arrows or the pointer are on, the pick checked at the end. The list scrolls with fading edges, so no row is cut off.
items.use_for: One choice from a list long enough to filter: a category, a brand, a board. With the filter off it is a plain listbox for a handful of options.
never: Many picks at once: it holds one value
Writing your own arrow, Escape or outside-press handling
A shadow under the panel, or a spectrum color on the highlighted row
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: the input's #666666 hairline and the brand corner for the trigger, the #262626 card fill and neutral hairlines for the panel, DM Sans 14px rows. shadcn's combobox (a popover and a command list) for anatomy and keys.
items.body:
The value is `value` with `onValueChange` (React) or the `value` property with `change` (web component). `pinned`
options stay above a hairline and are never filtered ("All formats").

items.name: coming-soon-page
items.title: Coming soon page
items.description: The site's coming soon page, built from library items: the page head with two buttons, the sources coming next as cards (a Black cover with the source's mark over clearing ASCII glyphs, the name, a line and the APIs it feeds as chips), the side drifts from 1440, the smaller cards also on the list, the closing section and the footer.
items.use_for: What a product adds next: sources, integrations or features that are planned, each with what it will feed. Edit lib/pages/coming-soon.ts or pass `content`.
never: Dates you cannot keep: say soon, not a day
Other companies' marks without their permission: pass your own through `mark`
Colored marks: they take the faint gray
items.source: Site app/products/coming-soon and pages/ComingSoon (ComingSoon.tsx, ComingSoon.module.css): cards on --surface, 8px in, covers 128, 160 from 768 and 240 for the first two from 1024 with the alpha texture at each card's --ascii-at and the radial clear, names h5 24/28, chips on --surface-inset; the also row four across from 768; PageHead, SideDrifts, PageClose; the platforms and their marks left out (named by kind here)
items.body:
A source is `{ name, line, apis: [{ name, href }], mark? }`; `mark` is an image URL (an SVG works best), shown through a
mask in the faint gray. Without one, a neutral rounded square stands in.

`sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`head`, `next`, `also`, `close`); a key left out is not shown.
`menus` passes the header menus (the live card's `picture`, the use cases' `shots`).

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.description: A box to type in over a list of actions and places, on the #262626 overlay surface: the field on top over a hairline, groups with a capital label, the menus' rows with an icon and a shortcut. On the page, or in a window opened with Cmd+K. The list scrolls with fading edges, so no row is cut off.
items.use_for: Jumping anywhere and running anything from the keyboard: searches, boards, brands, settings. CommandDialog for the app-wide Cmd+K menu.
never: Motion on opening or closing: it opens many times a day
Tab between rows: the field keeps focus and the arrows move
A spectrum color on the highlighted row
The only way to an action: keep it in the interface too
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: the #262626 card fill on Black, neutral hairlines, the 10px canvas corner (8px here), DM Sans 14px rows, capital labels at 6%. shadcn's command (cmdk) for anatomy, filtering and keys.
items.body:
Rows are data: `groups` of `{ heading, items: [{ id, label, keywords, shortcut, icon, disabled }] }`. In the web
component, a row's icon is page content with `slot="icon-<id>"`.

items.name: compare-table
items.title: Compare table
items.description: The site's plan comparison: a table per group, its head (the group's title and the plans' names) sticking under the page header while the group scrolls, then a row per line with a value in #A3A3A3, a White check or nothing for each plan. Names can carry a tip and a link, lines the Soon tag; on phones one plan at a time.
items.use_for: Under a pricing table, to compare plans line by line: usage, what each plan includes, access, support.
never: Colored checks or crosses: a plan without the line shows nothing
Long sentences in a cell: a value or a check
More than four plans: the cells get too narrow
items.source: Site pages/Pricing (CompareTable.tsx, CompareTable.module.css, Pricing.module.css .compare*): rows on a 2fr and 1fr grid, 24px apart, ruled by --line, 16px in; the sticky head at --header-h with the 48px fade; titles h4 to h3 at 1024; the dotted --text-3 underline and the tip on --raised after --dur-menu-intent; the phone picker is the segmented switch
items.body:
A cell is `true` (included, read out as "Included"), `''` (not included) or a short value. `labels` changes the words
for the tag and for assistive tech. The site hides the table on phones; it still works there, one plan at a time.

items.name: connect-menu
items.title: Connect menu
items.description: The site's connect menu: a White button that opens a panel of the agents your MCP server can be added to, each row with its mark or first letter, a muted line and Open, plus a row that copies a setup prompt for any other agent; a pill slides to the row under the pointer or focus.
items.use_for: A hero or a page head's main action when the product connects to agents (MCP); `up` near the foot of a page; pass `marks` and each client's `mark` only when you may show them.
never: Third-party logos without permission: by default rows show their first letter and the button shows no marks
A second White button beside it: pair it with a quiet one
Arrows that move on hover: they change color only
Shadows under the panel: it sits on a hairline
items.source: Site v3/V3Playground ConnectMenu (ConnectMenu.module.css, content/v3/connect.ts): the .btn--primary trigger at 12px in with a 16px chevron that turns over; the panel 8px under it, 336px (100% under 768), 4px in, #1A1A1A in a --line hairline with an 8px corner; rows 8px in with a 32px tile, 14/20 Medium name over a 12/16 --text-3 line; a hairline; the copy row 40px (48 on phones); the --surface sliding pill; 160ms in and 120ms out from scale 0.96. The library drops the panel shadow, keeps the arrow still, and opens at once from the keyboard

items.name: contact-page
items.title: Contact page
items.description: The contact page template, built only from library items: the heading and a line beside a form on the #262626 fill (name, work email, message, one White button), the header and the footer row.
items.use_for: A website's contact page. Edit lib/pages/contact.ts or pass `content`; the form posts to `content.form.action`, or `onSubmit` (the element's `send` event) takes the values.
never: An address, phone number or reply time you cannot keep
More fields than you need, or a second White button
New colors, shadows or type sizes added to a section: use the items' props
items.source: Built from the library (site header, field, input, textarea, button, footer row); the brand assets have no contact layout, so it follows the page templates and the plan card's fill
items.body:
`sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`intro`, `form`); a key left out is not shown. `menus` passes the
header menus (the live card's `picture`, the use cases' `shots`).

items.name: context-menu
items.title: Context menu
items.description: The dropdown menu's rows on the #262626 overlay panel, opened where the pointer right-clicks, or under the focused row with Shift+F10 or the menu key. Arrows, Home, End and Escape are handled; focus returns to what was clicked.
items.use_for: Shortcuts for a row in a dense list (open, copy a link, save, remove), alongside a visible way to do the same.
never: The only way to an action: right-clicks are hidden; keep a dropdown menu or a button in the row
Destructive actions that don't confirm: confirm with an alert dialog
A shadow under the panel
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: the #262626 card fill on Black, neutral hairlines, the 10px canvas corner (8px here). shadcn's context menu for anatomy and keys.
items.body:
Put `data-context="<id>"` on each row; `onOpen` (React) or the `open` event (web component) gets the id of the row
that was clicked, so one menu serves the list. `PopoverPanel` is the floating panel every overlay here draws (the
context menu, the combobox, the date picker): portalled, placed beside its anchor or the pointer, flipped to the side
with room.

items.name: creative-card
items.title: Creative card
items.description: A creative as the brand shows it: an ad, a product shot or a UGC frame in the brand corner, its color exactly as posted. Without an image it draws a neutral placeholder, so no layout needs a third-party photo.
items.use_for: Every creative on a page or in a view: search results, boards, the hero's row, a ring or a corridor. Pass the image as `src` (the user's own creative); the placeholder stands in until there is one.
never: A filter, a tint, a grade or neon over the image: color as posted
A border, a shadow or a glow around it
Another brand's photo in a template or an example: use the placeholder or the user's image
Moving or zooming on hover
items.source: Brand guidelines page 36 (Brand imagery: real creative, color as posted, on Black); Figma page 8: every Creative rounded rectangle (ads 4/5, the post's 200 squares, the ad's 296x400 three up, the ring's 160x114 and 112x146)
items.body:
`src` is used exactly as given: object-fit cover, no filter. Without `src` the card is a neutral gradient from two
neutral steps (`tone` 1 to 4) with the advertiser in capitals (from 112px wide) and a headline (from 192px wide), named
for assistive tech by `alt` or by those two. The arrangements (creative grid, row, ring and corridor) take the same
fields as a list.

`fit` and `position` place the image in the card (object-fit, cover by default, and object-position). The placeholder
carries `data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: creative-corridor
items.title: Creative corridor
items.description: Creatives as walls on both sides, receding in perspective to a small light at the vanishing point, in the ad's exact places.
items.use_for: The one picture of scale on a page: an index of every network, the depth of the archive. Headline above, a line of copy below.
never: Text over the corridor
A corridor that moves or scrolls
Two corridors on one page
items.source: Figma page 8: Ad, The world's largest creative search engine (Corridor L0 to L5 and R0 to R5, Light, end of corridor 140x104 at the vanishing point)
items.body:
Each picture is an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`); without `src` it keeps its placeholder, which carries
`data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: creative-grid
items.title: Creative grid
items.description: Creatives in a grid, every cell the same shape: the post's three by three of squares 8px apart with a light tile among them, or the ad's three up in 3/4.
items.use_for: A board, the results of a search, or the proof under a hero: many creatives at once, read as a set.
never: Cells of different sizes in one grid: use the creative row or the ring
More than one light tile in nine
A grid on a card
items.source: Figma page 8: Post, Any brand or creator (200x200 creatives 8px apart, a Light tile in the middle); Ad, The only creative search engine (three creatives 296x400, 32px apart)
items.body:
`items` takes the creative card's fields; `light: true` makes a cell a tile of the brand light (`seed` picks it).

Each picture is an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`); without `src` it keeps its placeholder, which carries
`data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: creative-ring
items.title: Creative ring
items.description: Twelve tiles around the middle of a square in the post's exact places: eight creatives, four tiles of the brand light, and the lockup inside.
items.use_for: A cover, a social post or the center of a section that says everything is in one place. The middle holds the lockup, nothing else.
never: A headline or a paragraph in the middle: only the lockup
Tiles moved off the post's places, or spun
items.source: Figma page 8: Post, Creative ring (1080x1080; creatives 128x128, 112x146 and 160x114; Light tile 112x145 and 128x128; Spyglass lockup 261x40 in the middle)
items.body:
Each picture is an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`); without `src` it keeps its placeholder, which carries
`data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: creative-row
items.title: Creative row
items.description: A row of 4/5 creatives: even, as the banners line them up 16px apart, or peak, rising to the middle and centered on one line, as the deck cover sets them.
items.use_for: A strip of proof beside a headline: a banner, a deck cover, the band under a hero. The row shrinks with its box and never scrolls.
never: A row that scrolls sideways: show fewer creatives
More than seven creatives in a row
items.source: Figma page 8: X banner, Creative row (six 120x150, 16px apart); Pitch deck cover, Row of creatives (200x250, 240x300, 304x380, 240x300, 200x250, 16px apart)
items.body:
Each picture is an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`); without `src` it keeps its placeholder, which carries
`data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: cursor-effects
items.title: Cursor effects
items.description: One cursor effect for the whole page on a fixed canvas behind it: a dashed trail of the brand light when the mouse flicks (the site's default), a soft circle of ASCII characters over empty page, or a burst of light chips where a thrown mouse stops. Clear of text, controls and pictures.
items.use_for: A marketing site's layout, once, under everything; with the ASCII lens for the drifts and the button glow.
never: More than one on a page
On touch, with reduced motion or forced colours
In a product screen, where the pointer is working
items.source: Site effect/PointerEffects, CursorSwitch (a trail, b lens, c burst), CursorTrail, CursorLens, CursorBurst and their cursor-*-effect.module.css: fixed, z -1, plus-lighter, shown for (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) without reduced motion

items.name: dashboard-page
items.title: Dashboard page
items.description: A product dashboard: a side rail, the title and one White button, four figures on cards and the latest rows in a hairline table.
items.use_for: The overview screen of the product; data comes through `content`.
never: New colors, shadows or type sizes added to a section: use the items' props
More than one White button in a view
Real people or customers in the copy: Acme only
items.source: Built from the library and the site's surfaces (cards on --surface, the rail on --raised, hairlines, the 36px links of the header)
items.body: `sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`head`, `stats`, `table`); a key left out is not shown.

items.name: data-table
items.title: Data table
items.description: A table people filter, sort and page through: a dropdown per filter, heads in capitals that sort, 40px rows on neutral hairlines that take the #262626 fill under the pointer, numbers in tabular figures, Previous and Next under it. It scrolls sideways with fading edges inside the frame.
items.use_for: A board's creatives, a brand's ads, a team's searches: rows of one kind of thing that people narrow and order.
never: Zebra stripes or a shadow: hairlines separate rows
Bold heads: DM Sans Medium capitals at 6%
A spectrum color for a sorted column or a picked filter
A table wider than the page without its own scroll
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: DM Sans for cells and capital labels for heads, neutral hairlines, the #262626 card fill for the hovered row and the filter menus, the 10px canvas corner (8px here). shadcn's data table (filters, sortable heads, pagination) for anatomy and ARIA.

items.name: date-picker
items.title: Date picker
items.description: A date in a field: a button drawn as the text field that opens the calendar on the #262626 overlay panel under it. Opening puts focus on the picked day, picking closes it and returns focus, Escape closes it unchanged.
items.use_for: A single date in a form: when a report starts, when a campaign ends. The field reads the day in words.
never: A shadow under the panel: the hairline and the #262626 fill set it apart
Typing a date into the button: it is picked from the calendar
A red edge for anything but an error
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: the input's field (40px, the 8px corner, a #666666 hairline that turns White on focus), the #262626 card fill for the overlay. shadcn's date picker (a popover holding a calendar) for anatomy and keys.
items.body: The web component is form-associated: give it a `name` and the form sends the day as an ISO date (2026-11-03).

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: A modal window on the #262626 overlay surface over a Black scrim: a Funnel Display title, a line under it, a ghost close button, a short form or an offer, and buttons at the foot.
items.use_for: A short task that needs the whole attention for a moment: naming a new board, an offer, a setting with a few fields. Escape, the close button and the scrim close it.
never: A long flow or a whole page in a window
Two primary buttons in the foot
A shadow or a glow around the window
Opening one with the page
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: the #262626 card fill on Black, neutral hairlines, the 10px canvas corner (8px here), Funnel Display titles, DM Sans text, the White primary button; the offer copy from the plan card. shadcn's dialog for anatomy, focus and keys.

items.name: direction
items.title: Direction
items.description: Sets the reading direction for what is inside it, so logical spacing and the components follow right-to-left text. Code stays left to right.
items.use_for: An interface in Arabic or Hebrew, or one block of right-to-left text inside a left-to-right page.
never: Mirroring the logo or the brand light
Flipping code, IDs or numbers
items.source: shadcn's direction provider; nothing visual of its own.

items.name: dispersion-field
items.title: Dispersion field
items.description: The brand light drawn live in WebGL: soft blobs of light bent by slow waves, split into Blue, Green and Red, with the ASCII ghost of the light around them, in one of the site's compositions. It drifts while on screen and brings a lens under a mouse; with reduced motion it is one still frame.
items.use_for: The light behind a hero, a closing band, the footer's wordmark or a product run, filling a positioned section behind the content; seeded so a page always draws the same field.
never: Under text people read: it sits behind the content, which keeps clear of its brightest parts
Boxed into a small card as an illustration
More than one live field in view
Moving with reduced motion, or the lens on touch
items.source: Site effect/DispersionField with engine.ts, layout.ts, shader.ts, drag.ts, stills.ts and lens.ts: 8 by 16 glyph cells from " .:-=+*#" at 0.35, blur step min(6, max(4, 0.3125vw)), 30 frames a second idle, lens radius 240, zoom 0.12, widen 0.5; compositions hero, close, band, frame, logo, crown, works, ring, horizon, wordmark, run; the works stills public/brand/light/field/works-*.webp from 1024; the per-width values the site's tokens set (the horizon's tilt 0.04 and cross 0.5 from 1024, the run's card, rise, offset, stage and depth from 768) read from the -md, -lg and -xl tokens

items.name: drawer
items.title: Drawer
items.description: A panel that slides in from an edge over a Black scrim, on the #262626 overlay surface: from the bottom with the brand corner on its top edge and a grab handle, or from the left or right at full height. The body's edges fade while there is more to scroll.
items.use_for: A choice or a short list on a phone (a format, a sort, the pages), where a dropdown would be cramped. The scrim, Escape and the close button close it.
never: A long form: use a page
A shadow on its edge: the hairline sets it apart
Corners on the edge it slides from
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: the #262626 card fill on Black, neutral hairlines, the 10px canvas corner (8px here), Funnel Display titles, 44px touch rows. shadcn's drawer for anatomy and behavior (no drag to dismiss yet).

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: Dropdown menu
items.description: A button that opens a short list of actions or choices on the #262626 overlay surface: a neutral hairline, the brand corner, rows that take a #262626 fill under the pointer. Arrows, Home, End, Escape and Tab are handled.
items.use_for: A creative's actions, a sort order, account actions: a handful of choices that don't need to stay on screen. Radio rows for one choice from a few.
never: Writing your own outside-click or arrow handling
A shadow under the panel: the hairline and the #262626 fill set it apart
A spectrum color for a row or its marker
Two or three views of one thing (use tabs)
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: the #262626 card fill on Black, neutral hairlines, the 10px canvas corner (8px here), DM Sans 14px rows and capital labels at 6%. shadcn's dropdown menu for anatomy and keys.
items.body:
`MenuItem`, `MenuLabel` and `MenuSeparator` are the rows of every menu here (the context menu uses them too); they are
also exported under shadcn's names (`DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`).

items.name: empty
items.title: Empty
items.description: What shows where a list has nothing in it yet: a dashed hairline with the brand corner, a Lucide icon in a #262626 tile, a Funnel Display title, one muted line and the actions that fill it.
items.use_for: A new board, a search with no results, a list before the first item.
never: Illustrations or the brand light inside it
An empty state with no way forward
A spectrum color for the icon
items.source: Derived from the guidelines: Funnel Display titles, DM Sans muted lines, the #262626 card fill, neutral hairlines and the brand's voice (short declarative sentences ending with a period). shadcn's empty for anatomy.

items.name: enterprise-features
items.title: Enterprise features
items.description: The site's enterprise features: a section head over eight cards, each a looping product sketch over a crop of the ASCII texture with its title and line (data layer, archive, agents, engineers, three teams, a built tool, shared reports, private answers).
items.use_for: What an enterprise plan includes, shown as working sketches rather than icons. One per page, after the proof.
never: Third-party marks or people's photos you may not show: pass your own through `content` (placeholders are first letters and neutral gradients)
Sketches that keep moving with reduced motion
More or fewer than the eight cards: the grid's 2-2-2 / 3-3 rhythm is built for eight
items.source: Site pages/Enterprise (FeatureGrid.tsx, FeatureGrid.module.css, Feature*.tsx, FeatureVisuals.module.css, FeatureAlpha.module.css, featureMotion.ts, reportsScroll.data.ts), v2/V2Features (Demo, timeline) and content/pages/enterpriseFeatures.ts: --ent-feat-* (16px gaps, 24px in, sketches 288px, 320 from 1024; loops on --dur-loop-step 2600ms); hairline rings drawn as outlines, no drop shadow under the cursors
items.body:
Each sketch is markup built once in `lib/enterprise-features-html.ts` (both flavors render the same tree) and played by
`runFeature` in `lib/enterprise-features.ts`: infinite Web Animations from a time of its own, only while a quarter of the
card is on screen and the tab visible. `content` carries every card's copy and data; pictures take `src` (else `tone`),
marks take `mark` (an image drawn White through a mask, else the name's first letter).

The sketches' pictures (`shot`, `ads`, `shots`) are image slots (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`; `crop` still works
for position); placeholders carry `data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: enterprise-hero
items.title: Enterprise hero
items.description: The site's enterprise hero: the headline, lead and two buttons centered in a hero at least the window's height, inside a ring of twelve creatives that rise in, bob while seen, come forward with a tag naming the hook, and step through their set on a press.
items.use_for: The head of an enterprise or sales page whose proof is the creatives themselves. One per page.
never: Third-party creatives you may not show: pass your own through `cards` (placeholders are neutral gradients)
More than one White button
Cards that keep moving with reduced motion
A ring around a long headline: the words keep a 216px room in the middle
items.source: Site pages/Enterprise (EnterprisePage .hero, Enterprise.module.css, HeroRing.tsx, HeroRing.module.css) and content/pages/enterprise.ts: min height max(640px, 100svh less the header); --ent-ring-* (cards 136 to 240px from the room, 128 on phones, 24px edge; forward 1.1 after 80ms; float 8px over 6s; a hint every 6s held 2s); the ASCII tiles from 1024 cleared 464px around the words; the entrance 480ms with a 40ms stagger and no blur (site 1500ms, 24ms, a 16px blur), the hover 320ms (site 300ms), the tag 160ms (site 150ms) and no shadow under a forward card
items.body:
`cards` takes up to twelve sets, clockwise from the top left (the two side places show from 1280, the six corner and
middle places on phones). Each card: `brand`, `title`, `ratio` (3:4, 4:5 or 1:1), `hook`, `meta` (the tag's lines) and
`src`; without `src` it is a neutral gradient with the brand. The tag finds room below, above or inside its card, off the
headline and inside the hero.

Each ring card takes `src`, `fit` and `position`; one without `src` carries `data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: enterprise-page
items.title: Enterprise page
items.description: The site's enterprise page from library items: the header, the hero inside its ring of creatives, the logo row, the automation run under its quote, the eight features and the close with two buttons, then the footer.
items.use_for: An enterprise or sales page; `content` replaces the copy, and `cards`, `logos`, `run` and `features` take your creatives and marks.
never: Customer logos, quotes or creatives you may not show: the defaults are Acme placeholders
A second White button in a section
The connect menu in the close: this page closes on a demo
items.source: Site app/enterprise and pages/Enterprise (EnterprisePage.tsx, Enterprise.module.css, LogoStrip.module.css) and content/pages/enterprise.ts: hero, logos (--ent-logos-above 24px, 16 from 768; --section-y below), AutomationRun, FeatureGrid, PageClose with two buttons and no texture
items.body:
`sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`hero`, `proof`, `run`, `features`, `close`); a key left out is not
shown. `cards`, `run` and `features` carry the pictures (image slots: `src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`). `menus` passes
the header menus (the live card's `picture`, the use cases' `shots`).

items.name: error-page
items.title: Error page
items.description: The site's error page: what shows when a page fails to render, the error head alone on Black (the title in one line, what happened in a plain sentence, the White Try again and the quiet way home), with no header or footer.
items.use_for: An app's or a website's error boundary (Next's error.tsx and global-error.tsx). Try again calls `onRetry` (React) or fires `retry` (web component).
never: An error code, a stack trace or a joke as the title
More than one White button in a view
The header and footer: the page that failed may be what draws them
items.source: Site app/error.tsx, app/global-error.tsx, pages/PageHead/ErrorHead.tsx and content/pages/errors.ts: the page head without the drift, the White retry beside the quiet homepage link; main's last section keeps --section-y under it
items.body: `sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`head`); a key left out is not shown.

items.name: faq-block
items.title: FAQ block
items.description: The site's FAQ: the section head, a lead and a quiet button on the left, held under the header while the questions scroll by on the right; one answer open at a time, the rows sliding to make room and the plus turning to a minus. `layout="stack"` puts the head over a narrow list. The rows also stand alone as FaqAccordion.
items.use_for: The questions section of a home, pricing, product or contact page (place it in a section with the page's padding); FaqAccordion alone where the page sets its own head.
never: Answers the product does not state
More than one answer open at once
Colored question marks or icons
items.source: Site v3/V3Faq, ui/FaqAccordion and v2/V2Faq V2FaqList (V3Faq.module.css, V2Faq.module.css): 4fr and 7fr columns 64px apart from 1024, the head sticky at the header plus 32px, centered on phones; .t-lead 24px under the head, the quiet docs button 32px further; rows under --line hairlines, 20px (24 from 768) above and below a 20/28 --text-2 question, a 12px plus of 2px strokes; the answer 16/24 --text-2 at 640px, 24px (32 from 768) under; slots sized to the longest answer, rows sliding over --dur-move on --ease-out; the v2 list centered at 640 + 80px with its hairline at the foot

items.name: feature-grid-block
items.title: Feature grid block
items.description: What the product does, as cards: an optional Funnel Display heading and line over a grid of cards on the #262626 fill, each a title and a sentence, three or two across.
items.use_for: The section of a home or product page that says what the product does, one card per job.
never: Icons, colored cards or images inside the cards
More than six cards, or a card without a sentence
Claims the product does not make
items.source: Built from the library (card); the home page's three cards (copy from Post, Know what changed; Post, Every market; Ad, One photo)

items.name: features-block
items.title: Features block
items.description: The home's features: a centered head and four cards in two columns, each a stage that shows the product working over its title and line: the media strip, the accounts burst, the graph ring and the patterns tally.
items.use_for: What the product gives, shown in four short scenes rather than listed.
never: Other companies' ads, logos or platform marks without permission: the defaults are Acme placeholders and plain names
More than four cards
The stages moving with reduced motion: each rests on one frame
items.source: Site v2/V2Features (V2Features.tsx and .module.css, MediaStrip, AccountsBurst with its data, ring and hook, PatternsTally, v2/V2Why GraphRing, v2/motion/findSimilar.ts and saveFromAnywhere.ts): two columns 32px apart from 768, 4/3 stages with the ASCII texture at their edges, titles 20/24 under them with 88px between rows (52 on phones); the strip's camera track at 30 fps, the burst's ring at 60, the ring's twist over 208 frames, the tally's reel glide 400ms and the read hold 2800ms
items.body:
Each picture is an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`); without `src` it keeps its placeholder, which carries
`data-ds-placeholder`. Each search in `burst` takes `images`, used in turn.

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description: A label over one control, with a description or an error under it. The label speaks in capitals; the help is muted; an error takes the help's place in red.
items.use_for: Every labeled control in a form: an email, a board name, a note, a pick from a list. One Field per control.
never: A placeholder in place of the label
A red hairline before anything is wrong: errors show once a field is left or the form is sent
Fields under 16px on phones (the input switches to 16px there)
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no form in the brand assets): the label voice from the type page, the neutral steps for help text, the red tints for errors

items.name: footer-block
items.title: Footer block
items.description: A website's footer band: a hairline above, the footer row (the lockup, links and the domain) inside the page width, and an optional legal line in the muted gray.
items.use_for: The foot of every website page.
never: A second logo, social icons in color or a newsletter box inside it
Links that move on hover
The lockup recolored or resized below its minimum
items.source: Built from the library (footer row); the posts' and ads' footer row (lockup left, domain right) and the page templates' footer band

items.name: footer-row
items.title: Footer row
items.description: The row every post, ad and deck ends on: the lockup on the left, the domain on the right. Links between them make it a website footer.
items.use_for: The foot of a page, a post, an ad or a slide. The domain in DM Sans, or in capitals as the posts set it.
never: The lockup on the right or centered with the domain
A colored or redrawn lockup
Social icons in place of the domain
items.source: Figma page 8: every post and ad's Spyglass lockup (183x28 at 64 or 72 from the edge) and spyglass.so text on one line; posts set the domain in capitals

items.name: form
items.title: Form
items.description: Fields stacked 24px apart, a failure from the server in a dark red box, and the actions at the end, the main one last. Errors wait until a field is left or the form is sent.
items.use_for: Any form with more than one field: tracking a brand, inviting a teammate, account settings. useForm holds the values, the rules and the send.
never: Errors while the first value is still being typed
The browser's own error bubbles
A red hairline at rest
Two primary buttons: one White action, the rest secondary or ghost
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no form in the brand assets): Field, Input and Button, the red tints for the failure, one White primary

items.name: hero-block
items.title: Hero block
items.description: The top of a page as the slides, posts and ads set it: a Funnel Display headline, a line of DM Sans and one White button on Black, with the light flowing in and the media (a search bar, a row of creatives) under the copy.
items.use_for: The first thing on a website page. Left with a search bar on a band of the light (the ad), centered under the light field (the offer post), or right-aligned over creatives on the curved strip (the deck cover).
never: A headline that does not end with a period, or in title case
Two White buttons
The light boxed in the middle of the copy, recolored or moving
Text over the creatives
items.source: Figma page 8: Ad, The only creative search engine (headline at 64,168, the line at 312, the search bar on a Light band); Post, Offer and Ad, Creator plan offer (centered under the Light field); Pitch deck cover, Curved strip (headline at the top right, creatives over the curved strip)
items.body:
`light` sets where the light flows: `field` from the top edge, `corner` from the bottom right, `band` across the media
and `strip` above it, or `none`. `texture` adds the ASCII texture behind it. The headline takes inline nodes in React
(the deck's creatives between the words) and a `headline` slot in the web component.

items.name: home-page
items.title: Home page
items.description: The site's home, from library items in its order: the header, the playground hero, the proof row, the features, the reasons, the set-up steps beside the MCP session, the case stories, the pricing strip, the questions, the close among the creatives and the footer.
items.use_for: A home page for a product agents use. Add it, then edit the copy in lib/pages/home.ts and lib/home/* or pass each block's content; the sections are library items you can reorder or drop.
never: Third-party customers, logos or ads without permission: every default is an Acme placeholder
New colors, shadows or type sizes added to a section: use the items' props
More than one White button in a section
items.source: Site app/page.tsx and app/v2/page.tsx (V3Playground hero, V3Proof, V2Features, V2Why, V2HowItWorks, V3CaseStories, V2Pricing, V3Faq, V3Close, the header and footer), measured at 1440 and 390; built from ascii-trail, playground-hero, proof-block, features-block, why-block, how-it-works-block, case-stories-block, pricing-panels-block, faq-block, close-block, site-header and site-footer
items.body:
`sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`hero`, `proof`, `features`, `why`, `steps`, `stories`, `pricing`,
`faq`, `close`); a key left out is not shown. `blocks` gives each block its own data, pictures included:
`hero.session`, `features` (`ads`, `burst` with each search's `images`, `ring`, `tally`), `why` (`creatives`, `logo`),
`steps.session`, `stories` (`cases` with each `picture`, `quotes`), `pricing.sets` and `close.creatives`. `menus`
passes the header menus (the live card's `picture`, the use cases' `shots`). Each picture is an image slot (`src`,
`alt`, `fit`, `position`); without `src` it keeps its placeholder, which carries `data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: hover-card
items.title: Hover Card
items.description: More about a link while the pointer rests on it: the card's #262626 fill, a hairline and the brand corner. The pointer can cross into it; on touch the link just works.
items.use_for: A preview of a brand, a creator or a board named in text, with a few numbers. The link must lead to the same thing on its own.
never: The only way to reach what it shows: the link must work on its own
Actions someone has to take: use Popover or Dropdown Menu
A shadow or a glow: the fill and the hairline set it apart
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no hover card in the brand assets): the plan card's #262626 fill and corner, the neutral steps for the hairline

items.name: how-it-works-block
items.title: How it works block
items.description: The home's set-up section: the headline, the lead, three numbered steps between hairlines, the connect menu beside the quiet button and the clients' marks, with the MCP session playing beside them from 1024.
items.use_for: Showing how to start in three steps, with the product answering a real question next to them.
never: Other companies' logos without permission: the default marks are first letters
More than three steps
Marks that move on hover: the others dim and the name appears
items.source: Site v2/V2HowItWorks (V2HowItWorks.tsx and .module.css, Session.tsx and .module.css, sessionClock.ts, content/v2/how-it-works): five to seven columns 64px apart from 1024, 48px stacked; steps 16px tall padding between hairlines with a 32px number column; actions 12px apart, 40px under the steps; marks 40px tiles 8px apart; the session stage 480px least, 40px in (24/16 on phones), the window's foot fading over 96px; the column drift at the left from 1440; on phones the connect menu hidden and the quiet button White (globals.css [data-mcp-pair])

items.name: input-group
items.title: Input Group
items.description: A field with an icon, a prefix, a unit or a small button inside its hairline, drawn and sized as the input is. The hairline turns White while the field has focus.
items.use_for: Fields that read better with their context attached: a search icon, a link's fixed start, a currency and its period, an invite button beside an email.
never: A primary search: use the search bar
Icons that do nothing at the end of a field
More than one button inside a field
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no grouped field in the brand assets): the input's hairline, fill and corner, and the search bar's button set inside the field

items.name: input-otp
items.title: Input OTP
items.description: A one-time code, one cell per character, each cell drawn as the input. It is one real field, so paste and the phone's code suggestion work.
items.use_for: Sign-in and verification codes sent by email or text. Say under it where the code went.
never: Passwords or keys
Cells that move focus on their own: it is one field
A colored or glowing cell for the one being typed: its hairline turns White
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no code field in the brand assets): the input's hairline, fill and corner, DM Sans for the digits

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: A text field on Black: a #666666 hairline that turns White on focus, DM Sans, a #A3A3A3 placeholder and the brand corner. Sizes match the button's.
items.use_for: Free text in forms and filters: an email, a brand or creator to track, a board name. Label every field (a visible label, or aria-label).
never: A placeholder as the only label
A colored or glowing focus ring: the hairline turns White
A filled or gray field on Black
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no field in the brand assets): the search bar's Black field and corner, the neutral steps for the hairline and placeholder

items.name: instrument-marks
items.title: Instrument marks
items.description: Four hairline corner brackets in the text colour around a target, a few pixels outside its edges, like a viewfinder locking on: the site's instrument mark for the item a figure is reading.
items.use_for: Marking the tile, figure or row a diagram is pointing at, in the site's instrument figures.
never: Around controls or text people read, as a focus or selection state
In a color: they are the text colour, hairline
items.source: Site instrument/marks (Brackets) and instrument.module.css (.brackets): inset -4px (--b-off), 8px arms (--b-arm), 1px hairline in --text, z 2

items.name: item
items.title: Item
items.description: A row: media, a title in DM Sans Medium with a muted line under it, and actions at the end. No fill, a hairline box or the card's #262626 fill. ItemGroup puts a hairline between rows.
items.use_for: A board, a tracked brand, a setting or a notification as one row; a list of them in a card. With href the whole row is a link.
never: Buttons inside a row that is a link
A chevron or arrow that moves on hover
A row of rows for many columns: use Table
A shadow under an outlined row
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no list row in the brand assets): the plan card's fill and corner, DM Sans Medium for titles, the neutral steps for the hairline and the muted line

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: A key: DM Sans 12px in the soft neutral, in a 20px #1A1A1A box with a hairline and the small corner. KbdGroup holds the keys of one shortcut.
items.use_for: Keyboard shortcuts beside the action they run (in a menu, a tooltip, a help list) and a key named in a sentence.
never: The only way to learn an action: the action must be visible on its own
Key names in capitals or in mono
Shortcuts shown on touch screens with no keyboard
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no key in the brand assets): DM Sans, the neutral steps for the box and its hairline, the small corner

items.name: label
items.title: Label
items.description: A field's label: DM Sans Medium in capitals with 6% tracking, in the soft gray, over the control it names. A muted hint can follow it.
items.use_for: Naming a field or a control when Field's layout does not fit: a label beside a switch, over a slider, over a group of radios.
never: A placeholder in place of a label
Bold, color or a spectrum accent on a label
Sentence case or long text in a label: say it in two or three words, and put the rest in a hint under the field
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines: labels in DM Sans Medium, capitals, 6% letter spacing (type page), the neutral steps for the gray

items.name: legal-page
items.title: Legal page
items.description: The site's legal pages (terms, privacy): the header, the page head with the title, the lead and the ASCII drift, then the text in the head's columns (the sections at the 640px measure on the left, their list staying in view on the right) and the footer.
items.use_for: Terms of service, privacy, cookies. `page` picks the terms or the privacy copy; `preparing` shows only the head, its lead saying the text is on its way (the site's state until the text is ready); the text is a placeholder: put what your counsel approves in lib/pages/legal.ts or pass `content`.
never: Shipping the placeholder text
Text set in gray or under 16px: the sections read in White at 16/24
A display-size title: the page head's section head
items.source: Site app/terms and app/privacy (AsciiTrail, Header, PageHead with the title and the 'being prepared' lead, Footer: the `preparing` state); the text in the site's type: .t-sub subheads (h6, h5 from 768), 16/24 paragraphs in --text at --measure, the page head's 7fr and 5fr columns; --section-y under it
items.body:
`sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`head`, `body`); a key left out is not shown. `menus` passes the
header menus (the live card's `picture`, the use cases' `shots`).

items.name: light-image
items.title: Light image
items.description: One of the site's pre-made light pictures (or your own) with the ASCII grain drawn where its light falls off into Black; with a mask, a mouse brings a lens that magnifies the light and widens its Blue, Green and Red split.
items.use_for: The light behind a hero or a pricing run, placed at an edge and behind the content, where the grain carries it into the page.
never: Under text people read: the lens and the grain sit behind the content, at the edges
A photo, a screenshot or a third party's picture as the light: it is for light art
Boxed in a card: the light bleeds off an edge
The lens on touch or with reduced motion: it stays the picture
items.source: Site effect/LightImage (LightImage.tsx, grain.ts, lens-gl.ts, LightImage.module.css) and effect/lens.ts: grain cells 8 by 16 from " .:-=+*#" at --ascii-trail-opacity 0.35, reach --light-grain-reach 64px, lens --light-grain-lens 192px; lens radius 240, magnify 0.12, widen 0.5, follow 14, ease 7; the art public/brand/light/hero-band.webp (2800 by 696) and pricing-light.webp with its mask (2640 by 1400, split 24); data-offscreen on the box while it is off screen when there is no lens (LightImage.tsx's IntersectionObserver)

items.name: logo-strip-block
items.title: Logo strip block
items.description: A row of customer names under a label in capitals, each set as a Funnel Display wordmark in the muted gray, so no third-party logo is drawn; their own marks go in the slot when you have permission.
items.use_for: Showing who uses the product, on a home or pricing page, with names you are allowed to show.
never: Third-party logos without permission, or recolored marks
Names of customers who have not agreed to be named
Motion or color on hover
items.source: Derived from the guidelines (Funnel Display, neutrals for muted text, labels in capitals with 6% tracking); no customer logos are in the brand assets, so the names are Acme placeholders

items.name: logo
items.title: Logo
items.description: Every lockup from the brand's own files, in Black or White: the logomark, the 3D logomark, the wordmark, and the horizontal, vertical and 3D combination marks.
items.use_for: The lockup at the top of a page, post or slide (183 by 28 on the 1080 canvas), the logomark where space is tight, the 3D marks for brand moments. White on Black is the primary; Black on White the secondary.
never: Stretched, rotated, recolored, outlined or with effects
A spectrum color on the mark: the colored backgrounds take a White or Black mark
Redrawn or retyped: use these files
items.source: Brand guidelines (Logo system); Figma page 8: Logomark, 3D logomark, Wordmark, Horizontal, Vertical and 3D combination marks; logo-horizontal.svg and logo-3d-horizontal.svg

items.name: mcp-session
items.title: MCP session
items.description: An AI chat asking an MCP server questions in turn: each typed at a typist's rhythm, the tool call and reply settling in, four creatives arriving one by one and the table's rows rising into place, then the next question.
items.use_for: Showing the product answering in an agent, beside set-up steps or in a hero.
never: Real brands' names or ads in the questions without permission: the defaults are Acme
Playing with reduced motion: it rests on the first answer
items.source: Site v2/V2HowItWorks Session (Session.tsx, Session.module.css, sessionClock.ts and the hero reference timings): 60 frames a second, the settle from 90% over 18 steps, the type fade over 6 frames, the rows rising from 68px on the reference curve, plays from a quarter on screen
items.body:
Each picture is an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`); without `src` it keeps its placeholder, which carries
`data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: menubar
items.title: Menubar
items.description: Menu triggers in a row: a Black strip in a hairline with the brand corner, triggers in DM Sans Medium, each opening a panel of rows in the card's #262626 fill. Arrow keys move along the bar and through the rows.
items.use_for: A tool's commands grouped under a few words, as in an editor: a board's actions, its view, its sharing. Three to five menus.
never: Site or app navigation: use the Sidebar or Navigation Menu
One menu alone: use Dropdown Menu
A spectrum color for the open trigger: it takes the #262626 fill
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no menubar in the brand assets): Black ground, the neutral steps for fills and hairlines, DM Sans Medium for triggers, the plan card's #262626 fill for panels

items.name: native-select
items.title: Native Select
items.description: The browser's own select, drawn as the input: a #666666 hairline on Black that turns White on focus, the brand corner and a muted chevron. Phones open the system picker.
items.use_for: A pick of one from a short, plain list in a form or a filter row: a platform, a date range, a sort order.
never: A list that needs search or custom rows: use Select
Options that do something at once: use Dropdown Menu
A filled or gray field on Black
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no select in the brand assets): the input's hairline, fill and corner, the neutral steps for the chevron

items.name: navigation-menu
items.title: Navigation Menu
items.description: A site's top navigation: triggers and links in DM Sans Medium, each trigger opening a panel of links in the card's #262626 fill. It opens under a resting pointer, switches at once between triggers, and opens at once from the keyboard.
items.use_for: The website's header: the product's parts, resources, pricing. A few entries, each panel a handful of links with a line each.
never: App navigation: use the Sidebar
Actions: use Dropdown Menu or Menubar
A chevron that turns or moves on hover
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no navigation menu in the brand assets): Black ground, DM Sans Medium for entries, the plan card's #262626 fill for panels, the neutral steps for fills

items.name: newsletter-block
items.title: Newsletter block
items.description: A newsletter sign-up on a #262626 card: the title, a line, an email field and the White button, small print under them.
items.use_for: A newsletter or waitlist sign-up at the foot of a page or a post.
never: A second White button
A pre-checked consent box
items.source: Built from the library (input, button) on the site's card fill

items.name: not-found-page
items.title: 404 page
items.description: The site's 404 page: the header, the page head with the title, what happened in a plain sentence, the White way home and the quiet way to the docs, the ASCII drift in the right columns, and the footer.
items.use_for: A website's not-found page. Edit lib/pages/not-found.ts or pass `content`.
never: A joke or an error code as the title
More than one White button in a view
A search or other controls in the head: two ways on, home and the docs
items.source: Site app/not-found.tsx and content/pages/errors.ts: Header, PageHead (margin, the cluster drift) with the homepage and the docs, Footer; as main's last section the head keeps --section-y under it (56, 76 at 768, 84 at 1024)
items.body:
`sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`head`); a key left out is not shown. `menus` passes the header menus
(the live card's `picture`, the use cases' `shots`).

items.name: offer-block
items.title: Offer block
items.description: The offer as the posts and the Creator plan ad close: a centered Funnel Display headline, the terms in capitals with concrete numbers and one White button, with the light flowing in around them or from the top over a plan card.
items.use_for: The last section of a page, or the pricing page's top: one offer, one action.
never: Terms without numbers
Two offers in one block
The light boxed in behind the headline
items.source: Figma page 8: Post, Offer (Stop screenshotting at midnight. at 404; $10 for your first month, then $20/month in capitals at 580; Button, Start Creator for 50% off 320x64 at 626); Ad, Creator plan offer (Light field 1080x612 over the headline and the plan card)

items.name: page-close
items.title: Page close
items.description: The site's closing section: a centered last head over its lines, a note in the soft gray, the connect menu with a quiet button (or a White and a quiet button), and from 1024 two ASCII drifts fading in at the corners.
items.use_for: The last section before the footer on any site page; `control={null}` (connect="false" in web components) for two plain buttons; `texture={false}` on a page that already has drifts nearby.
never: Two White buttons: beside the connect menu the button is quiet
A display-size head: it is the section head
Moving drifts

More than one White button

items.name: product-page
items.title: Product page
items.description: The site's product page, one template for every product: the header, the product hero running the product's questions over their results with the works light behind, the proof row, the feature rows with their product visuals, the comparison where the product has one, the pricing receipt, the questions with the docs button, the closing section and the footer.

never: Features without a visual: each row has a product visual kind
Results, people or brands you may not show in the hero or the receipt
A second hero or a second White button in a section

`lib/pages/product.ts` holds three products, one per kind of page: Creator search (filters and records, with the
comparison), Comments (threads and themes, no comparison) and Landing pages (pages and the links board). The site's
products, features, rates and questions are its own; the results in the hero and the receipt are Acme, shown as
figures. `live` puts the dispersion field over the hero's still, as the site draws it.

`sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`hero`, `proof`, `features`, `compare`, `pricing`, `faq`, `close`); a
key left out is not shown. Each feature's `data` is its visual's content (product-visual's `data` for its kind,
pictures included); the pricing rows' and the free row's `picture` (a src or an image slot) replaces the neutral
block. `menus` passes the header menus (the live card's `picture`, the use cases' `shots`).

items.title: Product pricing
items.description: The site's product pricing section. receipt (the site's): the head, the free note and two buttons beside a receipt of three records at the rate, the free row and the total in credits with what is left of the free month; open: the rate set large beside what is free; plans: what each plan buys at the rate; rate: the rate alone in a ruled card.
items.use_for: The pricing section of a product page, with the product's own rate and records.
never: A total that does not add up: the item counts it from the rate and the rows
Prices other than the plans you sell
Two White buttons
items.source: Site pages/Products/ProductPricing, ProductPricingReceipt, ProductPricingOpen, ProductPricingPlans (and their CSS modules, ProductPricing.content.ts): the receipt on --raised with --radius-m, 16px in (32 from 768), rows ruled by --line with 48px pictures (64 from 768) 4:5, the total under --line-strong in h5 (h4 from 768); copy 5fr to 7fr from 1024 with 64px between (96 at 1280); the rate in h1-alt, display-s at 768 and display-l at 1024

The receipt counts its total from `value` (the leading number, one credit by default) times the rows, and what is left
from `freeMonthly`. A row without `picture` shows a neutral block; the free row without one shows the empty frame with a
plus. `plans` reads the leading number of each plan's `credits` to say how many records it buys, and shows `after`
when there is none.

Each row's `picture` takes a src or an image slot; the neutral block and the free row's empty frame carry
`data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: product-visual
items.title: Product visual
items.description: The site's product visuals: the 4:3 stage of a product page's feature row, a #262626 panel with the ASCII field around its clear middle and one small looping scene of the product, picked by `kind`: records, adding an account, comment themes, filters narrowing a search, timelines, ranked sheets, the links board and the patterns switch.
items.use_for: The visual beside a feature on a product page (the site's ProductFeatures rows alternate the texture's position by row), or any section that shows what the product does in a few seconds.
never: Another brand's pictures, logos or people in the data unless you may show them: the defaults are Acme with neutral shapes
A scene that keeps moving with reduced motion: each rests on its resting step
Copy that is not the product's: the scenes show real fields and real values
Two visuals of the same kind side by side
items.source: Site pages/Products/visuals (AddAccount, AddCreator, BrandRecord, CollabsTimeline, CommentThemes, CommentThread, CreativeRecord, CreatorFilters, CreatorRecord, FilterNarrow, PageRecord, RankedSheet, TaggedRecord, TaggedTimeline, useLoopCycle), v2/V2Features (LinksBoard, PatternsSwitch, v2/motion/collaborate.ts), ProductFeatures.module.css .stage and .ascii, components/loopPacing.ts; the records use v2/V2Pricing PanelsMotion (lib/panels-motion.ts) in its reading pace
items.body:
`kind` is one of `brand-record`, `creative-record`, `page-record`, `creator-record`, `tagged-record`,
`comment-thread`, `add-account`, `add-creator`, `comment-themes`, `creator-filters`, `filter-narrow`, `posts-narrow`,
`collabs-timeline`, `tagged-timeline`, `media-mix`, `campaigns`, `pages-switch`, `links-board` and `patterns-switch`.
`data` takes that kind's shape (`ProductVisualDataMap[kind]` in `lib/product-visual-data.ts`; its defaults are in
`productVisualDefaults`): pass `picture`, `avatar`, `logo` or `src` where you may show an image, and leave them out for
a neutral shape. `texture` picks the ASCII field's position (0 to 3; `false` in React, `"none"` in web components, for
none). The stage measures its own width, so the same visual fits a phone, a half column or a wide row.

The loops follow the site's reading pace: a scene starts once it is on screen, holds its first step for 3.8s, then
changes and holds 2.8s each time; with reduced motion it stays on its resting step. The ranked sheets and the patterns
switch are tabs (arrow keys, Home and End move between them); pressing one stops the loop on that view. The links board
holds its composed frame before it starts clearing and building scene after scene.

Every picture in `data` (`picture`, `src`, `avatar`) takes a src or an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`);
the neutral shapes drawn in their place carry `data-ds-placeholder`.

never: Another brand's creative in a cover: pass the user's images as `src` or keep the Acme placeholders
Cards that lift, scale or move on hover: only the surface changes color
More than three columns, or a card without a link
items.source: Site pages/Resources (ResourceHub.tsx, Resources.module.css) and pages/UseCasesPage (UseCaseHub.tsx, UseCaseHub.module.css): cards 8px in on --surface with --radius-m, turning --surface-hover (160ms, ease-out); the cover 240px (320 from 1024; the use-cases hub keeps 240) 24px in on --bg with --radius-s; tiles 4:5, 12px apart, flex 0 1 --resources-tile-w 120px (use cases 80, 64 at 1024, 80 at 1280, 96 at 1440); the code in mono 14/20 with comments and marks in --text-3; text 16px in (24 on top from 768), h5 title, body line in --text-2, meta 14/20 in --text-3; 16px between cards, 48 before the rows; rows 20px tall padding (24 from 1024) with a 240px name column from 1024, the line in --text-off and the .t-badge
items.body:
Cards are links; a card whose `href` starts with `http` opens in a new tab. A row without `href` is plain text (a
resource that is not live). The use-cases hub passes each use case as a card: its creatives as the cover, the name as
the title, the line and who it is for as the meta.

Each picture is an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`); without `src` it keeps its placeholder, which carries
`data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: resource-list-page
items.title: Resource list page
items.description: The site's list of posts or guides: the header, the page head with the list's title and line, the entries newest first as hairline rows (date, title, line; with a `thumb`, a 16:9 picture on the left and the three lines stacked beside it), or a quiet panel with the empty note and the way back to all resources, then the closing section and the footer.
items.use_for: A blog, articles or guides index; `list` takes the entries (an empty list shows the empty panel), `content` the rest of the copy.
never: Cards in the rows: the list is hairline rows, with at most a small 16:9 thumbnail on the left
Dates in a local time zone: they read in UTC so every reader sees the same day
Real authors or customers in the copy: Acme only
items.source: Site app/resources/[slug]/page.tsx and pages/Resources (ResourceList.tsx, Resources.module.css .list, .row, .date, .rowTitle, .empty): rows 24px tall padding with a hairline under each, the date 14/20 in --text-3 in a 160px column 32px from the title from 768, the title 20/28, the line in --text-2; .rowThumb and .thumb: a 96px picture column 20px from the text (160 and 32 from 768), the picture 16:9 with --radius-s across the three lines; the back button full width below 768 (globals.css main a.btn); the empty panel --raised with --radius-m, at least 320px tall, 32px in, the note 20/28 and the quiet button 24px under it
items.body:
`sections` lists the sections to show, in order (`head`, `list`, `close`); a key left out is not shown. Each entry's
`thumb` is an image slot or a placeholder `tone`. `menus` passes the header menus (the live card's `picture`, the use
cases' `shots`).

items.name: resources-page
items.title: Resources page
items.description: The site's resources page: the header, the page head with its ASCII drift, the hub's linked cards (templates, docs with code, case studies) in two columns, the hairline rows of what is coming, the closing section and the footer.
items.use_for: A resources or learn index that links to templates, docs, case studies and writing; `content` replaces the copy.
never: Another brand's creatives in the covers: pass your own images as `src` or keep the Acme placeholders
Real customers or people in the copy: Acme only
A second White button in the hub: the cards are links on the surface

items.name: row-fan
items.title: Row fan
items.description: Big names, each a link, whose pictures fan out in perspective beside the name (from 1024) or below it when it is pointed at, focused, tapped or scrolled to the middle, travelling from row to row on a soft spring; a card opens with its title and meta.
items.use_for: A list of a few templates, products or use cases, each with a handful of example pictures, as the templates page sets its rows.
never: More than a few rows, or long names that wrap
Pictures of real people or other brands' ads in examples: pass your own
Travel and scaling with reduced motion: it fades
items.source: Site ui/RowFan and rowFanMotion, set as pages/TemplatesPage/TemplateCities (TemplateCities.module.css, --cities-* tokens): cards 72, 96, 128; names h4, h2, display-s; turns 18, 15, 12 degrees at 640px perspective; the travel curve --ease-cities-travel
items.body:
Each card is an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`); a card without `src`, or with a generated blank, carries
`data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: scroll-area
items.title: Scroll Area
items.description: A region that scrolls on its own with thin scrollbars: a #363636 thumb on a clear track. Native scrolling, so wheel, touch and keyboard all work; overscroll stays inside. An edge with more past it fades (fade-y, fade-x, fade-xy) instead of cutting rows off.
items.use_for: A long list in a short box (boards in a side panel) or a row of creatives that scrolls across. Give it a label so a keyboard can reach it.
never: Custom drawn scrollbars that break native scrolling
A scroll box a keyboard can't reach: give it a label
Hiding the scrollbar on content people need to find
A scroll box inside a scroll box going the same way
items.source: Derived from the brand guidelines (no scrolling region in the brand assets): the base layer's thin scrollbar in the neutral steps

items.name: scroll-story
items.title: Scroll story
items.description: The site's scroll story: a story in chapters told while the reader scrolls. From 1024 the stage pins and the pieces (creatives, a board, chips, a page, a thread, a profile, a result card) move on keyframes in a 1512x982 frame scaled to the content width while each chapter's words rise in; below 1024 or with reduced motion the chapters stack over still arrangements.
items.use_for: Showing how a use case works, step by step, on a use-case or product page. `story` takes the data (`storyFromShape` in lib/scroll-story.ts builds the site's five-chapter shape from its parts), or `preset` names an Acme story; `actions` are the last chapter's buttons.
never: Motion with reduced motion: the chapters stack and hold still
Another brand's ads, logos or channel marks shipped in the data: pass your own `src`, `mark` and logos, or keep the placeholders
More than one White button: the first action is White, the rest secondary
Easing or timers on top of the scroll: the scroll position is the clock
items.source: Site story/ScrollStory (ScrollStory.tsx, pieces.tsx, timeline.ts, types.ts, ScrollStory.module.css) and content/pages/useCaseStories (shape.ts and the stories): the --story-* tokens (tokens.css 820-836), pinned at (min-width: 1024px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), the frame scaled to min(content / 1280, height / 982), chapter words at 41.6% wide, 24/32/40 Funnel Display 450 headings with the 20/28 lead
items.body:
The story data is plain JSON: `chapters` (heading, text, side, mode, when they come in and leave, and the still
arrangement used when stacked) and `pieces` (a kind, a size in frame px and keyframes: `at` in chapters, x, y, scale,
opacity, badge and mark opacity, an ease). `storyFromShape` makes the site's shape from a board, a hero and five ranked
creatives, five chips, a focal piece (board, thread, page or profile), four creatives around it and a result card.
Creatives without `src` draw the neutral placeholder.

Each picture is an image slot (`src`, `alt`, `fit`, `position`); without `src` it keeps its placeholder, which carries
`data-ds-placeholder`.

items.name: search-bar
items.title: Search bar
items.description: The ad's search bar: a Black field with the brand corner, the prompt in White DM Sans and a White Search button inside it. Enter or the button runs the search.
items.use_for: The one search of a page or a product view: searching creatives, ads, brands and creators by asking in words. Usually the first thing on the page, often over the brand light.
never: Two search bars on one page
A colored search button: it is the White primary button
The search bar inside a card
items.source: Brand assets (Figma page 8): Ad, The only creative search engine: Search bar (952x88, radius 10, Black), Button, Search (136x56, 16px in), prompt in White DM Sans 24px

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: One choice from a short list, drawn as the field is: a Black field, a hairline that turns White while open, a chevron. The list opens in the card's #262626 panel, the chosen row checked. A long list scrolls with fading edges.
items.use_for: Picking one of a few known values in a form or a filter: a platform, an order, a plan. Label it as any field.
never: A list that needs a filter: use Combobox
Options that do something at once: use Dropdown Menu
A colored or glowing focus ring: the hairline turns White
